page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-24-lssd is a compute-optimized server instance featuring 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 12 physical Intel Xeon 6985P-C cores. Operating at a base speed of 2.3 GHz, this x86_64 architecture includes 90 GB of system memory, yielding 3.75 GB per core. The processor is equipped with a 504 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512). Storage is bundled directly with the instance, providing 1343 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity across four physical drives.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core performance, with Geekbench single-core scores and single-threaded gzip compression rates reaching top-tier classifications. Multi-core performance is robust, as demonstrated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 16269.0 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 27401.23. The memory subsystem delivers a read-only cached bandwidth of 2029.07 GB/sec for small blocks, though uncached large-block write speeds drop to 65.29 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, the hardware-assisted AMX instructions enable top-tier text generation speeds of 365.79 tokens/sec for small 135M LLM models, though performance falls to a poor 2.39 tokens/sec for large 70B models due to the absence of dedicated GPU hardware.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-standard-24-lssd provides high resource density by combining dedicated compute cores with high-speed local NVMe storage, reducing the need for costly external block storage attachments. However, the lack of a GPU represents a clear tradeoff, rendering the instance inefficient for large-scale deep learning training or heavy LLM inference. This server is highly suited for high-throughput web serving, database operations, text processing, and intermediate-scale compilation or decompression tasks.
